description: Work hard, till it makes sense
summary: AstroGuard is a browser-based prototype for reviewing astronaut health indicators when a connection is unavailable. It presents simulated heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, and sleep across three mission scenarios. A trend chart and alerts show which readings triggered each demo rule. Crew members can record how they feel in a check-in that stays on the device. After an initial online visit, the dashboard can reload offline. AstroGuard also includes a mission research panel with average hematocrit measurements from four Inspiration4 crew members, sourced from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository.
details:
AstroGuard demonstrates how an astronaut could review changes in health indicators and record context for later review during a loss of connectivity. The prototype runs in a web browser and uses React, TypeScript, and Vite.

The dashboard has three scenarios: Normal, Fatigue, and Elevated heart rate. In the Fatigue scenario, the app explains that 4.5 hours of simulated sleep triggered the short-sleep rule because it falls below the 6-hour demo threshold. The elevated heart-rate rule flags a sequence only when the three latest simulated samples each reach 100 bpm. These thresholds illustrate how the rules work and have no diagnostic role.

After reviewing a flag, the user can log an energy level and an optional note. The browser saves the check-in with the scenario and timestamp. A service worker caches the production dashboard after the initial online visit. We verified that the dashboard reloads offline in Chrome and retains access to scenario controls and saved check-ins.

The Mission research panel uses NASA OSDR study OSD-569. It averages hematocrit measurements from four Inspiration4 crew members at each of seven ground collection points before launch and after return. The panel credits the study and does not use those observations to trigger alerts.

Source code and setup instructions: https://github.com/Ancess392/AstroGuard
